headline: A D.C. Council committee held a hearing on how schools use AI and screen time, with more than 150 people signed up to speak.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a local hearing with no decision yet, but part of a wider debate on AI in schools.
importance_line: Students, parents and teachers in Washington's public schools could see limits on AI tools and screens, but the hearing only gathered views and no rule or vote is reported.
summary: A local TV report carried by AOL.com says that a D.C. Council committee heard testimony on Friday 9 Oct 2026 on how schools use technology and AI, with more than 150 people signed up to speak, as tech advocates say students must learn to use AI and critics call tools such as AI tutors experimental and unregulated. Hoodline, citing The Washington Informer, adds that a parent group is pressing for a pause on student-facing generative AI tools, and the hearing follows a Frederick County school board vote to ban student AI use.
notes: WUSA9 original (403) not readable; read AOL.com and Hoodline instead. AOL's text does not name the original outlet, so the entry is a desk entry (source AI News Desk) with both outlets named in the summary.
